source.title: Learning through atypical "phase transitions" in overparameterized neural networks
source.authors: Carlo Baldassi; Clarissa Lauditi; E. M. Malatesta; R. Pacelli; Gabriele Perugini; R. Zecchina

record.file_problem: The full paper text is present. Some figures are included without recoverable numeric values; those results are recorded as figure-only where applicable.
record.tranche_reason: The study varies model size and measures training and test error, and measures local energy around trained solutions. Its architectures, data, and local-energy measure differ from the versions’ specified setups.
record.gate_note: The paper reports results on widening networks and on local energy around solutions. Cited results and background discussion about double descent, sharpness, and other work are not extracted as rows. Some plotted values are not recoverable from the supplied text.
record.test_reason: The study measures training and test error as network size increases in new synthetic, MNIST-parity and CIFAR-10 settings, bearing on V2. Its local-energy profiles do not test whether magnitude-aware sharpness tracks or ranks generalization gaps as V7 specifies.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is broadly accurate. The central conclusion is that a second transition creates rare, solution-dense regions that efficient algorithms appear to access, while numerous sharp solutions persist. Numerical experiments support this scenario; extending it generally and proving attraction of algorithmic dynamics remain open.
record.recipe_differences: The experiments use teacher-generated synthetic data, MNIST parity labels on principal components, and CIFAR10; they study deep MLPs and CNNs as well as a tree committee machine, rather than the versions’ specified model and data settings. The study also emphasizes local-energy geometry and phase transitions.
record.method_sensitivity: Initialization changes the MLP generalization-error plateau and algorithmic threshold. SGD and ADAM reach training fit at different CNN widths. For the committee machine, SGD is slightly worse than fBP in generalization error, and fBP has flatter local-energy profiles.

fits_no_version.finding: Solutions have locally flat multiplicative-noise training-error profiles; committee-machine and MLP solutions become flatter with increasing size.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Increasing overparameterization can increase local robustness of fitted solutions to multiplicative weight perturbations.

record.problems: The realistic-network result values are largely presented in figures without numeric text values. Deep MLP tests use a reduced MNIST parity task; CNN tests use a specific five-layer architecture. Local-energy measurements do not establish a quantitative or ranked relation to the generalization gap.
record.rows_left_out: No additional applicable results left out. Results cited from prior work and theoretical/background claims about double descent are not this study’s own experimental results.

untested.parts: No paired natural-label and random-label experiment reports training fit and held-out accuracy under the same recipe.

The original one-hidden-layer setup and training to convergence are not replicated. The CNN uses a fixed 200-epoch budget and permits one training mistake. A test-error peak near interpolation is not established.
No matched convolutional versus fully connected comparison or test of local connectivity.
The fixed-recipe SGD–Adam comparison does not evaluate the specified limited-tuning protocol or recovery methods.

No test of magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps within a convolutional family, or comparison against norm- and margin-based measures. Reporting flatness alongside test error does not establish this relationship.
No removal of memorized examples followed by retraining.

missing.what: The binary random-feature model's own analytical width sweep predicts monotonically decreasing generalization error for zero-, fixed- and maximum-margin solutions and the zero-margin barycenter. Numerical SA and fBP results accompany these predictions. These results are absent from the record.
missing.locator: Section II, Fig. 2 left panel and accompanying text

record.verdict_notes: Remove the V7 limits_scope verdict: the missing gap-ranking test is untested, not evidence of a limitation. Do not infer support for R2–R3 from the existence of different generalization plateaus. No verdict is assigned to the missing Fig. 2 results pending separate rows.

versions.untested_parts: No paired experiment fits random labels and natural labels with the same architecture and recipe, then compares held-out accuracy.

The experiments do not use the specified one-hidden-layer ReLU networks trained without explicit regularization on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10. The MLP uses five hidden layers, parity labels on the first 10 MNIST principal components, and ADAM; the CNN is trained on CIFAR-10. The paper reports test error decreasing with width after the networks begin fitting, but does not isolate behavior precisely beyond the zero-training-error threshold.
No comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures trained from scratch tests their relative generalization.
The study compares SGD and ADAM on some architectures but does not test the optimizer generalization claim under matched tuning conditions or the listed recovery methods.
Batch size is not varied to test the large-batch generalization claim.

The study measures local energy around solutions using multiplicative noise and reports flatness alongside test error, but does not rank generalization gaps against magnitude-aware sharpness or norm- and margin-based measures, and does not establish a correlation across networks with similarly low training loss.
The study does not remove memorized examples and retrain.

rows.subject: overparameterized continuous tree-like committee machine
rows.stage_stated: trained with SGD with cross-entropy loss
rows.operation_detail: Measured average local energy by perturbing solution weights with multiplicative noise and measuring training error against distance.

conditions.value: P = 10005 patterns produced in D = 2001 dimensions

rows.measure: Average local training error profile versus Euclidean distance from a solution
rows.baseline: At small distances, flat profiles are reported for both SGD and fBP.
rows.value: Minima are generally sharper close to the threshold; the profiles are flat for small distances, and fBP profiles are flatter than SGD profiles.
rows.uncertainty: Profiles are averages; uncertainty not stated.
rows.locator: Section III, “Overparameterized tree committee machine”; Fig. 5
rows.note: The paper describes flatness and separately reports test error decreasing with N, but does not quantify or rank the relationship between perturbation tolerance and the train–test gap.
rows.check: Local training-error profiles in a committee machine do not measure V7's relationship between magnitude-aware sharpness and generalization gaps. Flatness alone is not partial observation of that relationship.
